clue.text: Recalled problem with one key set for clockwork instrument

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so the word for the problem is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a problem in arithmetic is a sum
one is the Roman numeral I
C is a musical key
a TV set is informally the box

explanation.surface: A mechanical instrument that keeps going wrong has been tuned to a single key.
explanation.definitionFit: A music box plays a tune from a pinned cylinder driven by a wound spring mechanism.

clue.text: Catch boy to return glove

indicators.note: to return means going back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to net is to catch
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy is told to catch the ball and give back the glove.
explanation.walkthrough: NET then TIM, the whole read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a glove with one section for all four fingers and another for the thumb.

clue.text: Walk fast, second time lift's gone

parts.note: a lift in a car is a ride
gone, as in left, is out

explanation.surface: Someone walks off quickly after missing their lift a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To stride out is to walk with long, brisk steps, so to move quickly on foot.

clue.text: Chancellor's a bit insincere, somehow concealing tax matters at first

indicators.note: concealing means the rearranged letters hide the two initials within them
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are rearranged
at first means only the opening letter of each word

parts.note: first letter of tax
first letter of matters

explanation.surface: The Chancellor is somewhat insincere, hiding things about tax at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of A BIT INSINCERE; that anagram, by 'concealing', holds TM, the initials of 'tax matters'.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK Chancellor of the Exchequer is a senior government minister who sits in the Cabinet.

clue.text: Stink raised by part of a play that's very rude

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in this down answer the letters for the stink read upwards

parts.note: BO, body odour, is a stink
a scene is a part of a play

explanation.surface: A rude scene in a play causes a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensively indecent, far beyond merely rude by the standards of decency.

clue.text: Religious leader and bishops, in the main, rejected Sunday opening

indicators.note: in tells us the bishops sit inside the other piece
rejected means turned back, so the word for the main is read backwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic name for the open sea
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two bishops are BB

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of Sunday

explanation.surface: A church leader and some bishops at sea refuse to hold a Sunday service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the open ocean, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the female superior of a convent of nuns, so a leader in religious life.

clue.text: Yelp after pan with no lid boiled over for cabbage and potato dish

indicators.note: after means the yelp word comes after the rest
over means the boiled word goes around the topless pan, holding it within

parts.note: a pot that bubbled has boiled

indicators.note: with no lid means the top letter of the word is removed

parts.note: pan with its first letter removed
a yelp is a squeak

explanation.surface: Someone yelps after a pan without its lid boils over while cooking a vegetable dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Bubble and squeak is a British dish of fried leftover cabbage and potato, named for the sounds it makes in the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubble and squeak is a traditional British fry-up of leftover mashed potato and cabbage.

clue.text: Each cross in margins voided questions

indicators.note: in means the cross letter sits inside the abbreviation for each

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

indicators.note: voided means emptied of its middle, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of margins

explanation.surface: An exam paper with every answer crossed out in the margins is void.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are sets of test questions; by metonymy the questions stand for the papers.

clue.text: See Democrat in constituency going ahead quietly

indicators.note: going ahead means the constituency part goes before the see in this down answer
in means the Democrat letter is placed inside the constituency word

parts.note: a parliamentary constituency is a seat
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, and a bishop's see

explanation.surface: A Democrat is seen running quietly for a constituency.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is a favourite crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedately means in a calm, unhurried and dignified way, close to quietly in manner.

clue.text: Reckons Dad's confused by drink

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: Dad, the apostrophe s standing for is
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Dad is muddled by too much drink when doing the sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Adds up means totals figures, and also makes sense; both fit reckons as calculates.

clue.text: Drum and bass on the never-ending radio outside

indicators.note: on means the bass letter is placed after the rest in this across answer
never-ending tells us the word the loses its final letter

parts.note: the with its last letter cut

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of radio
B is the music abbreviation for bass

explanation.surface: A drum and bass track plays endlessly on the radio outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat with a strong, steady pulse, as a drum does; both are verbs of rhythmic pounding.

clue.text: Vociferously moaned, fed up with old dining room furniture

indicators.note: vociferously means loudly out loud, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: to moan wearily is to have sighed, and fed up means bored; together these two words are said aloud

explanation.surface: Someone complained loudly that they were tired of the antique furniture in the dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGHED BORED spoken aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a long cabinet for serving dishes and storing crockery, a traditional piece in a dining room.

clue.text: Jeopardises aims when filled with rage

indicators.note: filled with means the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: aims are ends, as in ends and means
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Someone's goals are put at risk when they lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeopardise something is to put it in danger, which is to endanger it; both are verbs of risking harm.

clue.text: Index includes unknown composer

indicators.note: includes means the unknown letter is placed inside the list word

parts.note: an index is a list
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns; here Z

explanation.surface: A catalogue entry includes a composer whose identity is unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the nineteenth-century Hungarian pianist and composer of the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: Jack gets toes crushed crossing large crowd

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: crossing means the crushed toes straddle the large letter, holding it inside
crushed means the letters of toes are squashed into a new order

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Jack has his toes trodden on while pushing through a big crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges TOES into OSTE, and 'crossing' puts L inside it to give OSTLE after J.
explanation.definitionFit: To jostle is to push and shove, as people in a crowd do; here crowd is the verb meaning to press against.

clue.text: Humorous stage show's almost at capacity

parts.note: a stage show is a play

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: at capacity means full

explanation.surface: A comic stage production is nearly sold out.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful means light-hearted and teasing, close to humorous in tone; both describe joking behaviour.

clue.text: Represent self as endlessly tough, which is not true

indicators.note: represent read as re-present, set out again, so these letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of as is dropped

parts.note: a tough is a thug, as is a hood, short for hoodlum

explanation.surface: Presenting yourself as hard-bitten is a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represent' is read as re-present, to set out afresh, which is why it signals a rearrangement; 'tough' is a noun, a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is a lie or untrue statement, something not in accordance with fact.

clue.text: Worth wearing comfortable shoes to see flowers

indicators.note: wearing means the shoes are worn around the worth word, enclosing it

parts.note: Crocs are a brand of comfortable plastic clogs
worth or value is use, as in of no use

explanation.surface: It's worth putting on sensible shoes to go and look at the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocuses are small spring-flowering bulbs with cup-shaped purple, white or yellow blooms.

clue.text: Drew again, boxing ringleader so had another go

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the word for drew again holds the extra letter

parts.note: a match that is drawn again is retied
the leader of ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boxer drew again, so the bout was fought once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drew again' is RETIED, a tied match; 'boxing' puts R, read as ring-leader, the first letter of ring, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have retried is to have tried again, which is to have had another go at something.

clue.text: University college indeed cultivated reason

indicators.note: cultivated means worked over like soil, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: indeed contains the word deed, read here as in deed

explanation.surface: A university college is indeed a place where reason is cultivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' is read as in deed, supplying DEED; it goes into the anagram with U and C.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reach a conclusion by logical reasoning, so to reason as a verb.

clue.text: Play around with complex clue over a couple of days

indicators.note: complex means intricate and tangled, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two days are DD

explanation.surface: A solver toys with a tricky clue for two days.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CLUE with DD to get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuddle is to hold someone close fondly; play around with is a loose idiom for such affectionate fondling.

clue.text: Leaves twice, heading for uncle's house in France

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea, the leaves
tea leaves a second time gives tea

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of uncle's

explanation.surface: An uncle twice leaves for his house in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is read twice: once as CHA, slang for tea, once as TEA itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French country house or castle, typically on a large estate.

clue.text: Push in rudely to get off boat

indicators.note: rudely means roughly or crudely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shoves past others to disembark from a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To unship is to unload or remove cargo or passengers from a vessel; here, taking something off the ship.

clue.text: Crop off sign for island

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the crop is removed from the zodiac word

parts.note: Capricorn is a sign of the zodiac
corn is a crop

explanation.surface: A farmer's crop failure is a sign to quit the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples, famous as a resort.

clue.text: Note American Vice-President's rising irritation

indicators.note: rising means going upwards, so in this down answer the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: E is a musical note
Veep is the American informal term for a vice-president

explanation.surface: A memo from the US Vice-President shows growing annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeve is something that annoys, as in a pet peeve, so a source of irritation.

clue.text: RuPaul maybe agreed, sort of, to host question session at the end

indicators.note: to host is to hold, so the rearranged letters hold the question letters inside
sort of means a loose version, so the letters of agreed are rearranged
at the end means only the final letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter of session

explanation.surface: RuPaul apparently agreed to host a question-and-answer session to close the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges AGREED into DRAGEE, which hosts QU, and N from the end of 'session' completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: RuPaul is the American performer famous as a female impersonator and host of RuPaul's Drag Race; 'maybe' marks an example.

clue.text: Show's design caught at heart of story

parts.note: a spec, short for specification, is a design

indicators.note: at heart of means the caught letter sits in the middle of the story word

parts.note: a story is a tale
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A theatre production's design is caught up in the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle is an impressive public display or performance, which is a show.

clue.text: Record old church's age

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An ancient church's age is put on record.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of history marked by distinctive events, which is an age.

clue.text: Partner in game getting bored, becomes foul-mouthed

parts.note: in bridge North partners South, abbreviated S
bored means weary, tired of something

explanation.surface: A bridge partner gets fed up with the game and starts cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named after compass points, so a partner can be S (South).
explanation.definitionFit: Sweary is an informal word for full of swear words, so given to foul language.

clue.text: Dr Spooner's darling impudence is popular at kids' party

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial letters of the two words change places

parts.note: ducky is a British term of endearment, like darling
lip is cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark from a sweetheart goes down well at a children's party.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first letters of DUCKY and LIP. A lucky dip is a British party game where children pull a hidden prize from a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip is a game where children draw a wrapped prize at random, a common feature of British parties.
